# tenarium_plan (Resource)

A plan bundles features and limits that tenants subscribe to.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tenarium_plan" "pro" {
  id          = "pro"
  name        = "Pro"
  description = "For growing teams"
  features = {
    sso   = true
    audit = true
  }
  limits = {
    members   = 50
    api_calls = 100000
  }

  # Changes apply to new subscribers only: tenants already on the plan are
  # pinned to its previous revision on every update.
  grandfather_on_update = true
}

# An add-on: a plan stacked on another one with tenarium_tenant.add_ons.
resource "tenarium_plan" "extra_seats" {
  id     = "extra-seats"
  name   = "10 extra seats"
  limits = { members = 10 }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Short, stable plan identifier such as `free` or `enterprise`. Changing it replaces the plan.
- `name` (String) Display name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-form description.
- `features` (Map of Boolean) Feature flags granted by the plan.
- `grandfather_on_update` (Boolean) When true, every update of the plan first pins the tenants currently on it to its current revision (`grandfather`), so the change only applies to new subscribers. Pinned tenants show the revision in `plan_revision` and can be moved on with it. Changing only this attribute calls no API. Defaults to `false`.
- `limits` (Map of Number) Numeric limits (e.g. `members`, `api_calls`) granted by the plan.

### Read-Only

- `version` (Number) Version of the plan, incremented on every change and used for optimistic locking.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import tenarium_plan.pro pro
```
